valueSets.context: The operator list is data-type dependent, not fixed: it changes with the data type of the field chosen in C: Field/Value. THE SOURCE NAMES THREE OPERATORS AND THEN WRITES 'and so on' - this list is EXPLICITLY OPEN and must not be treated as the operator catalog.

Two more operator words appear elsewhere in the same file inside worked examples: 'Is Greater Than' (in 'Approved Amount Is Greater Than 1000' and 'Request Date Is Greater Than 9/30/02') and 'Equals' (in 'Employee Group Equals GermanGroup'), i.e. the same two operators in title case - recorded here as evidence of the case drift rather than added as extra values. The type-matching rule the driver must honour: 'The data type of the value must match the data type of the field.' and 'If the condition uses a second field, its data type must match that of the first field.'

valueSets.context: The shipped catalog of default approval statuses, which is the selectable set for a step's Initial Status BEFORE any tenant-created status exists. valueSets.sourceQuote: Table 4: Default approval statuses

(work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). The table's third column, Approval Action, is populated on only FOUR of the 13 rows (Accounting Review -> Approve, Auto Approved -> Auto Approved, Pending Approval -> Approve, Sent Back to Employee -> Send Back to Employee) and blank on the other nine; that column is recorded here and NOT emitted as a value set for step_approval_actions, because the corpus never says those are that field's options - see orphanCandidates.

valueSets.context: The approver-facing action list on the Add/Modify Workflow Step page. EXPLICITLY PARTIAL - the source hedges with 'such as' - and written in lower-case prose, so the on-screen strings are not established.
valueSets.sourceQuote: The approval actions outlined on this page dictate the actions an approver can make on an invoice that is awaiting approval, such as approve, reject, or send back to employee.
valueSets.notes: The roster left this field's validValues empty on the reading that the approver-facing list is never enumerated; it is enumerated, but only as a hedged 'such as' clause inside a Note, which is why it belongs in a value SET carrying its own openness caveat rather than in a flat validValues array. THE FIELD IS POPULATED FROM A HELPER PANE - 'From the Approval Actions helper pane, click an action that an approver can make to an invoice that is awaiting approval.' - so the full pane contents are tenant/provisioning dependent and cannot be derived from this corpus. HARD SEPARATION the same Note insists on: 'These approval actions are different from the Workflow rule approval actions, which designate an action to take once a workflow condition is met.' Do not merge these three with the five step-rule actions. Cardinality: multi-select for approver roles, and the Role field description makes selection mandatory for every non-System role - 'then you must select an action or multiple actions in the Approval Actions field.'

valueSets.context: MUTUAL-EXCLUSIVITY CONSTRAINT SET, not a picker list: a single workflow rule may contain only ONE action drawn from these three. Emitted as its own set because the constraint is invisible in a flat validValues array and a driver that ignores it hits a hard error.
valueSets.sourceQuote: A single workflow rule can contain only one of these actions:
valueSets.notes: WORDING DIFFERS FROM THE ACTION TABLE'S OWN ROW LABELS AND IS NOT RECONCILED: this list writes 'Skip step', 'Change approver', 'Send back to employee' in sentence case, while the Edit Action table in the SAME FILE labels the rows 'Skip Step', 'Change Approver', 'Send Back to Employee' (those title-case strings are what the roster carries in step_rule_action_name.validValues). Both are recorded; neither is corrected into the other. Failure mode if violated: 'You may have multiple actions, but they cannot conflict with each other. If the actions conflict with each other, an error message appears.' Worked example from the source: 'you can have a rule that says skip this workflow step when the invoice total is less than 25 USD, but to send an email when you skip. You cannot have a rule that states, "skip this workflow step and change the approver."'

valueSets.context: REPEATABILITY CONSTRAINT SET, the complement of the mutual-exclusivity set: a single workflow rule may contain MULTIPLE instances of these two actions, and they may combine with one action from the exclusive three.
valueSets.sourceQuote: A workflow rule can contain multiple instances of these actions:
valueSets.notes: A THIRD WORDING OF THE SAME TWO ACTIONS: 'Generate an exception' here versus the Edit Action table row label 'Generate Exception' in the same file, and 'Send email' versus 'Send Email'. Recorded, not reconciled. Together with the exclusivity set this gives the complete rule-composition law the automation needs: at most one of {Skip step, Change approver, Send back to employee}, plus any number of {Generate an exception, Send email}. The two lists partition all five actions with no overlap and no omission.

valueSets.context: A FOURTH WORDING of the same five-action catalog, this one stated on the Steps page as a cross-reference while warning that these are NOT the same as the step's own Approval Actions.
valueSets.sourceQuote: There are five standard approval actions for workflow rules: generate an exception, send an email, send back to employee, skip this step, and change approver.
valueSets.notes: FOUR WORDINGS OF ONE CATALOG ACROSS TWO FILES, ALL RECORDED, NONE RECONCILED: (1) title-case Edit Action table rows in work-with-the-step-rules-page-4c33cda0.md - 'Change Approver', 'Generate Exception', 'Send Back to Employee', 'Send Email', 'Skip Step' - which is what step_rule_action_name.validValues carries; (2) the mutual-exclusivity list; (3) the repeatability list; (4) this one. This wording is the only one that writes 'send an email' (with the article) and 'skip this step' (with the demonstrative), and it is the only enumeration of the five that lives OUTSIDE the Step Rules topic. It also fixes the count at five, which corroborates that the Edit Action table has no sixth row. The same sentence is the corpus's explicit firewall against merging this catalog with step_approval_actions.

valueSets.context: SECOND, CONFLICTING READING of the Role catalog: the distinct Role values actually used by the two workflows SAP ships, in order of first appearance. Recorded alongside the Add Workflow Step page's own list rather than merged with it.
valueSets.sourceQuote: In the table below, the Role column defines the type of user that takes action at this step.
valueSets.notes: THE CONTRADICTION, STATED AND NOT RESOLVED. Reading A (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md, carried in step_role.validValues) enumerates System, Authorized Approver, Invoice Approver, Invoice Processor, Invoice Processor Manager, Invoice Vendor Manager - and is itself an OPEN list, hedged 'If it is a non-system role, such as Authorized Approver, ...'. Reading B, here, ADDS 'Employee' - a value reading A never offers - and OMITS 'Authorized Approver' and 'Invoice Processor Manager'. Neither list can be derived from the other. The most likely explanation, UNPROVEN from this corpus, is that 'Employee' denotes the submitter at the Payment Request Submitted system step rather than a selectable Role option; a driver must probe rather than assume. 'Invoice Vendor Manager (a System role)' is transcribed exactly as the table cell writes it, parenthetical included, even though the parenthetical is almost certainly documentation gloss and not the on-screen string - normalising it would be inventing a UI string. Semantics from the same file: 'If no approvers are involved, then the role is System. If the role is marked System, then Concur Invoice moves the invoice along to the next step automatically without human interaction.' and, for the Vendor Approval step, 'For the Vendor Approval step, the Role is a System role.'

valueSets.sourceQuote: An invoice workflow always consists of at least three steps, but additional steps may be added:
valueSets.notes: INTERNAL DISCREPANCY INSIDE THE SOURCE, CARRIED NOT SMOOTHED: the sentence says 'at least three steps' and the bullet list that immediately follows contains FOUR. valueSets.context: The complete data-variable catalog that may be typed into an email body. A STRUCTURED catalog, not a picker: every row of the source table yields a LABEL form and a VALUE form of one variable, and the label form is the value form with 'L_' inserted after the opening percent sign.
valueSets.sourceQuote: Field Label: %L\_WhoChanged%
valueSets.notes: ALL 18 DISTINCT VARIABLES, IN SOURCE ORDER, NONE SAMPLED. ESCAPING - A DELIBERATE, FLAGGED TRANSCRIPTION DECISION: the markdown source writes every underscore escaped as backslash-underscore (the sourceQuote above preserves that exactly, which is why it reads '%L\_WhoChanged%'), but the backslash is markdown escaping, not a character of the variable. The values array therefore carries the UNESCAPED strings a user actually types, which is what the automation needs. STRUCTURE: eleven table rows in two labelled sections - 'Invoice or Purchase Request Change' (Changed By, Request Name*, Request Date, Submit Date, Total Amount, Approval Status of the Workflow Step, Pay Status = 7 rows) and 'Invoice or Purchase Request Pending Approval' (Report From, Report From, Request Name, Total = 4 rows). Eleven rows yield 18 rather than 22 distinct variables because %L_RequestName%/%RequestName% and %L_Total%/%Total% appear in BOTH sections; and two different rows share the Field label 'Report From' while carrying DIFFERENT variables (%EmpName% = 'The name of the user who owns the invoice', %SubmittingUserName% = 'The name of the user who submitted the invoice'). The asterisk on 'Request Name*' resolves to the table's own footer row, which the markdown escapes the leading asterisk of: '\*These fields use the configured form field label, if available, instead of the default label.' SEMANTICS from general-information-00eca1ce.md: 'The variables are enclosed in percentage signs, which indicate to the system that they need to be replaced.', 'Adding an “L” (L) and underscore (\_) to the beginning of the variable name tells the system to replace that variable with the field label.', and 'NOTE: If the variable is blank, then both label and value variables will not print in the resulting email.' DO NOT SOURCE THIS CATALOG FROM email-notifications-8b3dbad4.md, which is a 61-row revision history containing exactly one variable.

valueSets.context: The same data-variable catalog, wired to the Email Subject field as well: the corpus states explicitly that variables work in the subject line, not only the body.
valueSets.sourceQuote: Field Value: %WhoChanged%
valueSets.notes: EMITTED AS A SECOND SET RATHER THAN FOLDED INTO email_body's, because appliesToField is singular and the subject-line applicability is separately attested rather than assumed. GROUNDING FOR THE SUBJECT: 'Data from the invoice can be added to the email subject or body text, using data variables.' (general-information-00eca1ce.md) and, in the procedure itself, 'Make the desired changes to the Email Subject field. You can use "variable" fields to enter specific data in this field.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md, where that sentence occurs twice - once on the Primary Recipient step and once on the Delegate Recipient step of the wizard). Same escaping caveat as the email_body set: the source escapes underscores as backslash-underscore in markdown; the values here are unescaped. Same 18 variables, same source order, same file. A subject line is plain text, so the HTML affordances that apply to the body (rich-text toolbar, Source Edit button) do not apply here.

valueSets.context: feature name = Invoice Vendor Employee Access. A ONE-VALUE SET, and that is the honest answer: SAP documents exactly one Level value here and states in the same breath that it cannot be changed.
valueSets.sourceQuote: Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).
valueSets.notes: NO SECOND VALUE IS IMPLIED AND NONE WAS ADDED. Completing a plausible pair is the exact defect that already cost this graph two deleted values, and it is refused here. DIRECTLY CONTRADICTED by the Invoice Payment reading ('Set the level to Request.'), which is emitted as its own set and NOT reconciled with this one: if Level were a single global control, 'cannot be changed' and 'set the level to' cannot both be true. The most likely - but UNPROVEN - cause is that the Level control's options vary with the selected feature hierarchy, in which case both statements are locally true. Whether 'cannot be changed' is a property of THIS hierarchy or of the first Level row of EVERY feature hierarchy is UNDETERMINED from this corpus. Immutability does not mean a single row: step 7 of the same procedure permits more - '(Optional): If you intend to use multi-level named vendor groups (Level 1; Level 2; Level 3) add additional levels and segments now to match.' - and the count is dictated by the chosen source list, 'If a multi-level list was created, be sure to add additional levels and segments to match the list levels.' Level rows pair one-to-one with Segment Name rows.

valueSets.context: feature name = Invoice Payment. A second ONE-VALUE SET, from the payment-groups/funding-accounts procedure. Recorded ALONGSIDE the Invoice Vendor Employee Access set, deliberately not merged and not reconciled.
valueSets.sourceQuote: Set the level to Request.
valueSets.notes: Step 6 of an 8-step procedure whose steps 5-8 are 'Select New.' / 'Set the level to Request.' / 'Select the custom field configured to the selected source list.' / 'Select Save.' - the same New / Level / Segment / Save sequence as the Invoice Vendor Employee Access procedure, with a DIFFERENT Level value and NO immutability claim. THE CONTRADICTION IS THE FINDING: do not infer that Employee and Request are both offered under either feature, and do not infer a combined two-value option list - no documented list enumerates them together. Corroborating but NOT sufficient to settle it: 'By default, the Request Authorized Approver hierarchy uses the Request and Employee fields' (admin-guides/understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md) shows Request and Employee coexisting as hierarchy field sources in a THIRD feature, which is why neither value was promoted to the field's own validValues. Precondition the driver must satisfy first: 'The source list and custom field referenced in the steps below must already be configured before you proceed.'

valueSets.context: feature name = Invoice Routing. The three invoice HEADER fields the source designates as the hierarchy path segments. A PREFIX-ELIDED enumeration: the source writes the word 'Custom' once and then three bare numerals.
valueSets.sourceQuote: three invoice header fields (Custom 10, 11, and 12) have been designated as segments to make up the full hierarchy path.
valueSets.notes: COMPRESSED-RANGE HANDLING: the source's own string is 'Custom 10, 11, and 12' - ASCII commas, an Oxford 'and' before the final member, NO dash or en-dash of any kind - and it is preserved verbatim in the sourceQuote. The values array carries the EXPANSION because it is load-bearing for automation: '11' and '12' are not field names, 'Custom 11' and 'Custom 12' are, and a driver reading the string literally would hunt for a field called '11'. The expansion is mechanical and every member is given explicitly by the source; nothing is inferred. THESE ARE THE SOURCE'S EXAMPLE CHOICES, NOT MANDATED FIELD NUMBERS - 'In the example below, the source list "sample" is selected' frames the whole passage as an example. COLLISION WITH A DIFFERENT CUSTOM FIELD ON THIS SAME PAGE: the Invoice Vendor Employee Access procedure uses Custom 02 as its Segment Name ('In the example below, Custom 02 is renamed to Choose Vendor Access Group', step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md), and that is an EMPLOYEE form field, where Custom 10/11/12 here are INVOICE HEADER fields. Same control, different form, different numbering - do not treat either set as required configuration. Cascade behaviour the segments produce: 'when a value is selected in the first field, the next field shows only those values the first field supports (Sales > North).' LABEL DRIFT: professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md calls this same control 'the custom field' rather than Segment Name.

valueSets.context: AN ATTESTED-NAMES CATALOG, NOT A DOCUMENTED OPTION LIST. No file in this corpus enumerates this selector's options; these are the three named feature hierarchies that separate topics explicitly describe as being SELECTED on, or configured through, the Feature Hierarchies page.
